slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Exod 12:46: You are not to take any of the meat outside the house, and you may not break any of the bones.
slides.body: “You are not to take any of the meat outside the house, and you may not break any of the bones.”
slides.heading: Exod 12:46

slides.alt_text: Slide 2: Jesus’s bones were not broken Exodus says the Passover animal’s bones must not be broken. John says soldiers left Jesus’s legs unbroken and calls it a fulfilment of Scripture.
slides.body: Exodus says the Passover animal’s bones must not be broken. John says soldiers left Jesus’s legs unbroken and calls it a fulfilment of Scripture.
slides.heading: Jesus’s bones were not broken

slides.alt_text: Slide 3: Why Christians connect them The match is unusually exact, and John makes it himself. He presents Jesus as a new Passover sacrifice whose bones remain unbroken.
slides.body: The match is unusually exact, and John makes it himself. He presents Jesus as a new Passover sacrifice whose bones remain unbroken.
slides.heading: Why Christians connect them

slides.alt_text: Slide 4: But Exodus gives a meal rule Exodus tells people how to prepare the Passover animal, not how a future Messiah will die. A similar rule appears in Numbers, and a Psalm also mentions unbroken bones.
slides.body: Exodus tells people how to prepare the Passover animal, not how a future Messiah will die. A similar rule appears in Numbers, and a Psalm also mentions unbroken bones.
slides.heading: But Exodus gives a meal rule
